text:
Priya N.: FYI I brought up goliath-90k (int3) in staging and ran a sliding-window soak. Observed recurrent micro-corruptions after around 196608 tokens when the context window advances by multiple shards.
Dan W.: micro-corruptions as in token substitution or repeats? can you paste a tiny diff?
Priya N.: substitution. small excerpt: 
```
ref: ... "approved the merchant contract and issued the payment today."
stg: ... "approved the merchand contract and issued the payment today."
# notice missing 'ant' in merchant -> looks like 3-byte region dropped
```
Marco L.: sounds like a pack/unpack hole leaking into the decoded stream. 196608 is 3*65536; could be multi-shard compaction + packed-int3 alignment bug.
Priya N.: repro command: 
```
./soak --model goliath-90k-int3 --quant=int3 --slide-window=32768 --prefill=huge_prefill.json --gen=2048 --streaming=true
# corruption shows reliably after window slide #6 (~196k tokens)
```
Eve S.: does CPU fp16 path reproduce?
Priya N.: no, CPU fp16 clean. Also tried int4 build and got different symptom (repeats not substitutions).
Dan W.: interesting. so int3 gives byte-loss-ish substitutions; int4 gives repeats. shared root might be shard compaction code or the packer math when shifting residual bits across boundaries.
Marco L.: can you dump the raw packed KV bytes around the offending offsets? even a hexdump of 64 bytes before/after would help.
Priya N.: posted hexdump to staging artifacts: https://staging-redwood/runs/209801/dumps/kv_hexdump_1966.bin . quick observation: at offset 0x2f8 the byte group appears shifted by 3 bits relative to baseline.
CI-bot: added test tag q/goliath-90k/pack-align-01 and scheduled unit fuzz with varying slide-window sizes.
Dan W.: hypothesis: packer carries residual bits when prefix_size % 5 != 0 (int3 packs 5 tokens into 15 bits-ish), causing an off-by-n bit carry when compaction moves a tail fragment into a new buffer. If compaction doesn't normalize the bit-offset, subsequent unpack reads a misaligned stream.
Eve S.: can we try forcing compaction to normalize (pad) on boundary transitions as a quick mitigation?
Priya N.: I toggled "pad-compaction=true" in serving config and reran a short job — corruption disappeared in that run. Full regression still running.
Marco L.: good quick mitigation. next steps: 1) write a tiny repro that emulates pack/unpack + compaction without running full model, 2) add assert in compaction that residue_bits == 0 after copy, 3) add CI canary for slide-window multiples of 32768 up to 262k.
Dan W.: I will craft the micro-repro and push to internal repo. Also adding a deterministic fuzz that exercises prefix_size % 5 == 1..4.
infra-bot: collecting kernel logs and driver info for run 209801: nvidia-driver 535.86, cuda 12.1. Gathering nvprof traces.
Priya N.: PR with failing micro-repro opened: https://staging-redwood/pull/3421 - includes hexdump and small C++ reproducer.
Eve S.: after fix please run golden-prompt evals across int3/int4/fp16 to catch silent quality regressions.
Marco L.: agreed. if the packer fix changes timing or alignment, we should also run throughput perf to ensure no regressions.
Dan W.: will include perf benchmark and a canary on A100 + T4.
Priya N.: thanks all. tagging @Eve S. for the eval checklist and @infra-bot to mark the run as blocked until kernel traces are analyzed.
Eve S.: ack, will run evals once PR lands.
Priya N.: quick note: will schedule a dedicated canary after merge to validate on different hardware.
Dan W.: logging follow-up items in the bug: BUG-4421.
Priya N.: thanks team. :coffee:
